clue.text: Become and stay a scapegoat

parts.note: to fall, as in 'fall ill', is to become
a guy is a rope or wire that stays a tent or mast

explanation.surface: Someone told to take the blame and keep on taking it.
explanation.definitionFit: A fall guy is the person set up to carry the blame for others, exactly what a scapegoat is.

clue.text: More like a Persian shopkeeper

explanation.surface: A carpet dealer from Iran.
explanation.walkthrough: The Persian is a long-haired cat, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A Persian cat is very furry, so one more so is furrier; a furrier is also a trader in furs.

clue.text: With fires round me, I'm cheerful

parts.note: fires are lights
O is round in shape
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone happy to be surrounded by fires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like a container signal but just supplies O; 'With' and 'I'm' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Lightsome means light-hearted, merry and carefree.

clue.text: He's bought it, one pound from 9's sister

indicators.note: the letters are taken away from the sister's name

parts.note: Regan's sister in King Lear is Goneril
I is the Roman numeral one
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A shopper spends a pound on something from his sister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bought it' is slang for died, so he is a goner.
explanation.definitionFit: A goner is someone dead or doomed, and to have bought it is slang for being killed.

clue.text: Measure of credit of the Metropolitan Police

indicators.note: the possessive of the police puts it before the credit word

parts.note: Scotland Yard, the Yard, is the London Metropolitan Police; 'of' gives the possessive S
tick is British slang for credit, as in buying on tick

explanation.surface: A judgment on how creditable the London police are.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotland Yard, 'the Yard', is the headquarters of London's Metropolitan Police.
explanation.definitionFit: A yardstick is a standard used to judge or measure things.

clue.text: Airman's set on to search around in Australia

parts.note: FO is a Flying Officer, an RAF airman, and the possessive adds S
to sick (or sic) a dog is to set it on to someone

explanation.surface: A pilot is urged to go rummaging about in the outback.
explanation.walkthrough: FOSSICK is Australian slang for rummaging, originally for gold in old diggings.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australian usage to fossick is to rummage or prospect about, a regional word for searching.

clue.text: "Concentrate', people said to us

indicators.note: said out loud, the word for people gives the first syllable

parts.note: folk means people
us taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone told to concentrate by people speaking to them.
explanation.definitionFit: To focus is to fix one's attention, a synonym for concentrate.

clue.text: Replace with one imprisoned beggar

indicators.note: the numeral is shut up inside the other word

parts.note: to supplant is to replace
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A beggar swapped for a jailed convict.
explanation.definitionFit: A suppliant is someone who humbly asks or pleads, much as a beggar does.

clue.text: Picture, for example, a road running north

indicators.note: in a down clue going north means reading upwards, backwards

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first motorway, written MI

explanation.surface: A snapshot of a road heading north.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the main motorway north out of London; 'running north' reads EG A MI upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a picture or likeness.

clue.text: Course prepared here for king on Hampshire river

indicators.note: in a down clue, the king sits on top of the river

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
the Itchen is a river in Hampshire, England, flowing through Winchester

explanation.surface: A king sets off on a course along a river in southern England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' is a course of a meal, not a racecourse or river's course.
explanation.definitionFit: Meals and their courses are cooked in a kitchen.

clue.text: King's daughter showing uncontrolled anger

indicators.note: anger that is out of control runs wild, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A royal princess is in a temper.
explanation.walkthrough: The king is King Lear; Regan is one of his three daughters, notorious for her cruelty.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's tragedy, Lear's second daughter bears this name.

clue.text: Alpine music factory

parts.note: rock is a genre of popular music
a plant is an industrial works or factory

explanation.surface: A mountain-side works turning out records.
explanation.definitionFit: An alpine is a small plant suited to rockeries, a gardener's name for this sort of flower.

clue.text: Enters mistakenly into its concerns

indicators.note: the scrambled word goes into the middle of the other word

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something done mistakenly is jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone muddles their way into a matter that is its own business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistakenly' turns ENTERS into NTERES, which goes 'into' ITS after the I.
explanation.definitionFit: One's interests are the matters one cares about or has a stake in, synonyms for concerns.

clue.text: One needing blood donors left with community hospital

parts.note: EEC is the European Economic Community
H is the map and sign abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A hospital appeal for blood donors, set in a European community.
explanation.definitionFit: The bloodsucking worm feeds on the blood of its hosts, which donate unwillingly.

clue.text: Mathematical function including pole or perch

indicators.note: one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: a square root is a mathematical function
S stands for the south pole

explanation.surface: A maths problem about a pole or a perch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is just a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: A roost is where birds settle to rest, a synonym for a perch.

clue.text: Sweet pea, sticky hybrid

indicators.note: a hybrid is a cross, so the letters are mixed together

explanation.surface: Gardening talk: a sticky new sweet pea variety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet pea' looks like one phrase, but 'Sweet' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipsy cake is a trifle-like dessert soaked in wine or sherry, a pudding or sweet.

clue.text: Copy — one atom in it is different

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: the letters of the words are made different by rearranging them

explanation.surface: A physics claim that a duplicate has one atom altered.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR text mangled the clue; the page shows a dash after 'Copy'. 'is different' makes MITATION from the letters of ATOM IN IT.
explanation.definitionFit: An imitation is a reproduction of something, the same thing as a copy.

clue.text: Landlord, last in 22

indicators.note: one word goes inside the other

parts.note: the answer to 22 down
to last is to keep, as food keeps

explanation.surface: A pub landlord coming last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last' looks like a position but is the verb meaning endure.
explanation.definitionFit: An innkeeper runs a pub or inn, which makes him its landlord.

clue.text: I am being treated without tolerance

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm
a patient is someone being treated by a doctor

explanation.surface: Someone under treatment who has no patience.
explanation.definitionFit: Impatient means unable to tolerate delay or annoyance.

clue.text: She records, with unusual ink and parchment

parts.note: taken as written
EPs are extended-play records

indicators.note: unusual ink is ink in an odd arrangement, so its letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A woman with old records and strange ink, writing on parchment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' turns INK into KIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Parchment was made from the treated skin of a sheep or goat, so a sheepskin is parchment.

clue.text: Smack has a course to steer …

parts.note: soup is a course of a meal
to con a ship is to steer it

explanation.surface: A sailing vessel with its course set.
explanation.walkthrough: A smack is a fishing boat on the surface, but here it means a slight taste, a smack of something. The ellipsis links into the next two clues.
explanation.definitionFit: A soupçon is a tiny trace or hint of a flavour, as is a smack.

clue.text: Subject to right of choice? Not quite

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: not quite the whole word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: the pick is the right of first choice, as in 'take your pick'

explanation.surface: A query whether something is subject to one's right to choose.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is the subject under discussion; the two are synonyms.

clue.text: … privateer needs breeze to follow one, we hear …

indicators.note: this word says the answer is heard rather than seen: it sounds like the word it governs

parts.note: breeze is AIR, following 'one', a course, carried over from the clue before

explanation.surface: A pirate ship needs wind behind it, so it is said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' refers back to 'a course' in 18 down: COURSE then AIR, spoken, gives the pirate.
explanation.definitionFit: A corsair was a pirate or privateer, especially of the Barbary coast.

clue.text: One Miss Mitford

explanation.surface: A single member of a famous family of sisters.
explanation.definitionFit: Unity means oneness, the state of being one; Unity Mitford was one of the famous Mitford sisters of 1930s Britain.

clue.text: … and several never started, to this man's detriment

indicators.note: the meal word never started, so its first letter is gone

parts.note: several courses, carried over from the earlier clues, make a dinner

explanation.surface: A tale of courses that never arrived, to someone's cost.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: an unstarted dinner harms the 'inner man', the stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: The inner man is an idiom for one's stomach or appetite, the one who suffers when a meal never comes.

clue.text: Warder's no vegetarian

explanation.surface: A Tower guard confesses he eats meat.
explanation.walkthrough: Beefeaters are the Yeoman Warders who guard the Tower of London; read literally the word means someone who eats beef.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tower of London's yeoman guards bear this nickname, and a beef-eating diner is plainly a meat lover.

clue.text: Spoil by holding up as well

indicators.note: the outer word holds the reversed one

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means read backwards

parts.note: too means as well

explanation.surface: Damaging something by delaying it as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns TOO into OOT, which BY holds.
explanation.definitionFit: Booty is plunder or loot, the spoils taken in war.

clue.text: More direction on "X" pictures coming up

indicators.note: in a down clue the direction sits on top

parts.note: E, for east, is a compass direction
taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: art is pictures and paintings

explanation.surface: Further guidance about X-rated films being released.
explanation.walkthrough: X was the old British certificate for adult films; here it is just the letter. 'coming up' makes TRA.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means additional, a synonym for more.

clue.text: Fruit from Natal chopped in ice-cream, out east

indicators.note: the chopped letters go in the middle of the dessert word
the compass letter is taken out of the dessert word

parts.note: a coupe is an ice-cream dessert served in a stemmed glass
E is the compass abbreviation for east

indicators.note: chopped up, the letters are cut and rearranged

explanation.surface: A fruit dessert from Natal, sliced into an ice-cream with no eastern touch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopped' turns NATAL into ANTAL; 'out' takes E from COUPE, leaving COUP, and ANTAL goes 'in' it after the C.
explanation.definitionFit: The cantaloup is a variety of melon, a kind of fruit.

clue.text: Letter that E changed into?

indicators.note: the letters are changed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about what an E turned into.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR dropped the E that the page prints. 'changed' rearranges THAT plus E; 'into?' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth character of the Greek alphabet, so it is a letter.

clue.text: Shark, a fish without a breeding ground

parts.note: the nurse shark is a kind of shark, called a nurse for short

indicators.note: the fish is taken without the letter, so it is removed

parts.note: a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: A shark and another fish have no place to breed.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR text lost both 'a's that the page prints. 'without' removes the second 'a' from RAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursery is a place where young fish or plants are raised, a breeding ground.

clue.text: Divine, without a breeding, ground

indicators.note: ground up, the letters are broken and remade in another order

parts.note: the Creator is God, the divine being

explanation.surface: A divine figure lacking good manners has been brought down to earth.
explanation.walkthrough: A companion to 27: the definition is playful, since a breeder reactor without its breeding is just this. 'ground' rearranges CREATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A breeder is one kind of nuclear plant; strip away the breeding and what remains is the plain device.
